plain.text: Four kings from the east went to war against five kings of the cities of the plain, including Sodom and Gomorrah. The kings of the plain were defeated, and some fell into tar pits as they fled. The invaders took all the goods and food of Sodom and Gomorrah, and they also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who was living in Sodom, along with his possessions.

A man who had escaped told Abram. When Abram heard his relative had been taken captive, he called out the 318 trained men born in his household and chased the invaders as far as Dan. He divided his men and attacked them at night, defeating them. He recovered all the goods and brought back Lot and his possessions, together with the women and the other people.

The king of Sodom came out to meet Abram. Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brought out bread and wine and blessed Abram: "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth. And blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand." Abram gave him a tenth of everything. The king of Sodom offered Abram the goods, but Abram refused: he had promised the LORD that he would not take even a thread or sandal strap, so no one could say, "I made Abram rich." He asked only for what his men had eaten and the share of his allies.

summary.bigIdea: Abram rescues Lot, is blessed by the mysterious priest Melchizedek, and refuses to get rich from the king of Sodom.
points: Lot is taken captive in a war between kings.
Abram rescues him with a small band of men.
Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, blesses Abram, and Abram gives him a tenth.
summary.reflection: Abram refused rewards so that only God would get the credit for blessing him. How do you handle credit and reward?
